Worked solution

There are three possible orders in which exactly two {@colour1@} balls can be drawn:

  • {@colour1@}, {@colour1@}, {@colour2@}

    \[\frac{@n1@}{@total@}\times\frac{@n1-1@}{@total-1@}\times\frac{@n2@}{@total-2@}={@pro@}\]

  • {@colour1@}, {@colour2@}, {@colour1@}

    \[\frac{@n1@}{@total@}\times\frac{@n2@}{@total-1@}\times\frac{@n1-1@}{@total-2@}={@pro1@}\]

  • {@colour2@}, {@colour1@}, {@colour1@}

    \[\frac{@n2@}{@total@}\times\frac{@n1@}{@total-1@}\times\frac{@n1-1@}{@total-2@}={@pro2@}\]

    • Add the probabilities of the three mutually exclusive outcomes:

    \[(\text{Probability of exactly two} \;{@colour1@}\; \text{balls})={@pro@}+{@pro1@}+{@pro2@}={\displaystyle {@ta1@}}\]

    Therefore, the probability of drawing exactly two {@colour1@} balls is

    \[ \boxed{{@ta1@}} \]
